steps.label: Germplasm collection defined
steps.margin_note: The full definition plus what it includes.
lines: A GERMPLASM COLLECTION is the entire collection
of plants or seeds having ALL THE DIVERSE
ALLELES for ALL GENES in a given crop.
It includes wild relatives, landraces and modern
steps.why: A breeder can only work with alleles that exist somewhere, so the collection is the whole pool of what is possible.
common_mistakes: Saying it is a collection of the best varieties. It is a collection of ALL the diversity.
Leaving out wild relatives. They carry most of the useful disease resistance genes.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.margin_note: Its place in breeding, and why loss is permanent.

lines.text: You can only breed with alleles somebody has

lines: It is a PRE-REQUISITE for any breeding programme:
the first of the five steps in releasing a new
An allele that is not in the collection cannot be
bred into a crop, and once a wild population is
lost its alleles are gone for good.
steps.why: Extinction is irreversible, so a wild relative lost today removes options from every future breeding programme.
common_mistakes: Giving no significance. The second mark is for why it matters.
Saying collections can be rebuilt later. Once a wild population is lost, its alleles are lost.
steps.memory_tip: Lose the wild relative and you lose the allele for ever.
